summary: Could not judge this core. The compile list I was given has only the MiSTer top level, the T80 CPU, a generic dpram wrapper, and the hiscore and pause helpers. The board's own logic sits in the entity naughty_boy (instantiated at Arcade-NaughtyBoy.sv:226-267) and its submodules under rtl/ (naughty_boy.vhd, naughty_boy_video.vhd, naughty_boy_effect1-4.vhd, naughty_boy_noise.vhd, tms3615.vhd, prom_palette_*.vhd). None of those are on the list, so I did not open them. Everything I was allowed to read is shared library or framework code, which the rubric says to treat as neutral, so this is a placeholder verdict, not a structural finding.

findings.signal: board logic not in reviewed file set
findings.note: The top level hands all game logic to the entity naughty_boy (clock_12, dn_* ROM download, 2-bit video_r/g/b, audio, dip_switch, player buttons). That entity's source is not in the given compile list, so its structure was not reviewed.
hps_io, arcade_video, screen_rotate, the PLL and the OSD config string are standard MiSTer scaffolding and say nothing about the board.

findings.signal: pixel clock enable from fast clock
findings.note: ce_pix is clk_44 divided by 8. This is ordinary FPGA clock-enable engineering.
OSD status bits are packed into an 8-bit dip_switch word (lives, bonus, difficulty, cabinet). Any correct core shares this with the emulator.
T80 is a shared Z80 library and is ignored under ground rule 2.
dpram is a plain altsyncram wrapper. hiscore and pause are generic MiSTer community modules. None of them carry board-specific logic.
